content.title: Adopt-a-Trail
content.summary: The Adopt-A-Trail program in Arvada allows individuals, companies, and groups to adopt sections of trail for a year, starting June 1, with responsibilities including monthly litter clean-ups. Participants receive a starter kit and recognition signs, while safety guidelines are provided to ensure safe litter collection practices. Interested parties can adopt trails marked with blue dashed lines on the interactive map available on the city's website.
content.body:
![Little Boy in Work Gloves](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=711 "Little Boy in Work Gloves")

## How Adopt-a-Trail Works

- Through the Adopt-A-Trail program, short sections of trail are adopted by individuals, companies, schools and other groups.
- Trails are adopted for a 12-month period starting June 1. Renewal notices are sent out each year in April.
- The adopting party enters into an agreement with the City of Arvada, stating that they will be responsible for picking up litter along a specified portion of trail for a period of one year.
- We request that trail adopters participate in a litter clean-up on their section of trail once per month.
- The Parks Department provides a starter clean-up kit and posts signs along the adopted trail, giving recognition to individuals or group volunteers.

## How to Adopt a Trail

If you would like to adopt a trail, please fill out the [Adopt-A-Trail program request form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/32095).

**Only trail routes labeled with blue dashed lines on the**[**Adopt-A-Trail map**](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=7e566dd161614b16bb5fa2aa5fbea4f0)**are available for adoption.**

## Available Trails

Trail sections that are available for adoption marked with blue dashed lines in our interactive Adopt-A-Trail map displayed below. [View the interactive Adopt-A-Trail map in a separate window](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/sidebar/index.html?appid=7e566dd161614b16bb5fa2aa5fbea4f0).

    iFrames are not supported on this page.

## Adopt-A-Trail Safety Tips

Please view these very important safety tips before you begin your litter pickup. If you are leading a volunteer group, please print the [safety tips (PDF)](/DocumentCenter/View/712) and distribute them to your volunteers. Thank you.

### List of tips that you should do:

- Schedule your litter pickups during the daylight hours and stop picking up litter before dusk.
- Watch the weather forecast and reschedule your pick up day/time during inclement weather such as thunderstorms and snow storms or during wet and/or icy conditions.
- Wear light or bright colored protective clothing, hard-soled shoes and sturdy work gloves.
- Use sunscreen and wear a hat.
- Drink fluids on hot days and rest if you get tired.
- Carpool to pick up sites to keep the number of vehicles on the roadside to a minimum.
- Park off the roadway as far away from the pavement edge as possible and use parking lots and wide spots when available.
- Keep children and pets safe while at your location. Never leave them in your vehicle.  .
- Stay alert for traffic when crossing roads and driveways. Use crosswalks when possible.
- Stay alert for snakes and noxious weeds and do not touch them.
- Use a stick picker/reacher/grabber tool if possible to avoid touching hazardous materials. These can be purchased at local hardware stores or online. If using your hands, always use protective gloves and be careful where you put your fingers. Avoid reaching into places where you can’t see objects you are touching.
- Leave trash bags along the route where they are easily visible for the Parks crew. Items such as hubcaps, wood, tires, etc., can be piled on top of the bags.
- Email [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#354147545c5946755447435451541b5a4752) for a trash pickup request with a specific location.
- Make sure all volunteers are familiar with these safety tips. (Responsibility of group coordinator)

### List of tips you **should not** do:

- **Don’t**pick up litter on roadways, in construction or maintenance sites, or in tunnels.
- **Don't**pick up or handle any dead animals. Instead, contact Arvada Animal Management at 720-898-6850.  For urgent animal concerns, contact 720-898-6900.
- **Don’t**overfill trash bags; partially filled bags are preferable to ones that are overfilled.
- **Don’t**try to pick up litter in fast moving water, on slippery rocks, steep banks, where water runs under roads, or any other area that may be dangerous.
- **Don’t**pick up materials that you suspect might be hazardous or dangerous.
- **Don't**drink alcohol or consume other controlled substances during litter pickups.
